ex: Our collie helps the farmer move the sheep.
A collie is a very smart and friendly dog.
Our collie has long, soft fur, so we brush it often.
Can we take the collie for a walk in the park?
We saw a burlesque show in a small club.
The burlesque dancers wore bright, funny costumes.
Burlesque shows mix comedy, music, and dance.
She took a burlesque dance class just for fun.
The family asked the church to send an exorcist.
The exorcist prayed in the old house all night.
The movie is about a young priest who becomes an exorcist.
In the story, an exorcist tries to help a sick girl.
This shirt is made of cheap polyester.
Polyester dries very quickly after you wash it.
The jacket is half cotton and half polyester.
I don't like polyester because it feels hot in summer.
The finale of the show was really amazing.
Everyone on stage sang together in the grand finale.
The fireworks were a perfect finale to the festival.
Did you watch the season finale of that series last night?
The illustrator drew all the pictures for this children's book.
She works at home as an illustrator for magazines.
The illustrator likes to paint with watercolors.
The writer and the illustrator met to talk about the cover.
I like to eat kimchi with rice and eggs.
Kimchi is a spicy Korean dish made from cabbage.
She makes her own kimchi at home every fall.
This kimchi is too sour for me.
The aorta is the biggest blood vessel in the body.
Blood goes from the heart into the aorta.
The scan showed a problem with his aorta.
Doctors did surgery to fix a weak spot in her aorta.
Our basset has very long ears and short legs.
The basset slept in the sun all afternoon.
A basset can smell things from very far away.
Is your basset friendly with other dogs?

impulse.note: Most often "impulse" means a sudden wish to do something: "I bought it on impulse."

la.note: Most often "la" is a sound in songs ("la la la") or part of names like LA. The note is usually called "A".
ex: Sing the notes do, re, mi, fa, sol, la.
In this song, the high note is la.
La comes after sol and before ti.
Can you play la on the piano for me?
The dingo is a wild dog that lives in Australia.
We saw a dingo near our camp last night.
Dingoes often hunt together in small groups.
Please keep your food away from the dingoes.

fundraiser.note: Most often "fundraiser" means an event to collect money: "a school fundraiser."
ex: She works as a fundraiser for a children's charity.
The hospital hired a fundraiser to find new donors.
Our best fundraiser collected ten thousand dollars this year.
As a fundraiser, he calls many people every day.
She wears a ring with a small amethyst.
An amethyst is a purple stone used in jewelry.
I bought amethyst earrings for my mom's birthday.
The necklace has a large amethyst in the center.

podium.note: Also the stand a speaker talks from. A fashion show walkway is a "runway," not a podium.
ex: The three winners stood on the podium.
She finished on the podium in all three races.
He hopes to get on the podium this year.
Only the top three runners stand on the podium.

mozzarella.note: Uncountable: "some mozzarella" or "a ball of mozzarella."

ex: Stress and lack of sleep can lower your libido.
This medicine may affect your libido.
Regular exercise can improve your energy and libido.
The doctor asked about changes in her libido.

condominium.note: Often shortened to "condo" in everyday speech.

ex: Our team keeps all its notes on a wiki.
I added a new page to the company wiki.
Please check the wiki for instructions.
Anyone on the team can edit this wiki.

all-in.note: Usually "go all-in": bet all your money in poker, or put all your effort into something.
ex: He went all-in with a pair of aces.
She pushed all her chips forward and went all-in.
Going all-in on the first hand is very risky.
If you go all-in and lose, you are out of the game.

coming out.note: Often written "coming-out". The verb is "come out": "He came out to his parents."

full house.note: Also means every seat is full: "The band played to a full house."

check-out.note: Also written "checkout". In a store, the "checkout" is where you pay.

ex: The coach always teaches the kids about fair play.
The team won an award for fair play.
Fair play is more important than winning.
Pushing another player is against the rules of fair play.

music hall.note: Mostly British: an old kind of show with songs and comedy, or the theater for it.

ex: I put a sandwich and an apple in my lunch box.
Her lunch box has a cartoon cat on it.
Don't forget to take your lunch box to school!
He left his lunch box on the bus again.
